transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Honestly, I'm here because I've been having a really hard time with talking too much. I constantly find myself interrupting people or blurting out answers before they even finish speaking, and it's starting to cause some real issues in my daily life.
Do you also have trouble paying attention, like getting easily distracted, losing things, or having a hard time finishing tasks? Or is it mainly the interrupting and blurting things out?

It is definitely mainly the interrupting, blurting things out, and talking too much. I don't really have issues with losing my things or getting easily distracted, as those don't seem to be my problems at all. It's just that I can't seem to stop myself from jumping into conversations.
Have these interrupting and blurting-out behaviors been present since childhood, like before age 12? Or did they start later in life?

Yes, they've been happening for as long as I can remember, definitely since well before I was 12. I vividly remember my elementary school teachers constantly writing on my report cards that I talked too much and wouldn't stop interrupting the class.
Do these behaviors cause problems in more than one setting, like both at work or school and at home or with friends? Can you give one example?
I'm not really sure if it affects multiple areas of my life, as I haven't really thought about it that way. I can't think of any specific examples across different settings right now.
Have your interrupting and blurting-out behaviors caused problems in at least two places, such as at work or school and also at home or with friends?
I'm really not sure if it causes problems in multiple areas like that. I haven't really thought about whether it affects both work and home, so I can't say for certain.
Besides talking too much and interrupting, do you often feel restless, have trouble staying seated, or act without thinking?

I definitely struggle a lot with talking too much, interrupting people, and blurting out answers before they're even finished. However, I don't really experience physical restlessness or have any trouble staying seated.
Do you often act without thinking in other ways too, like making hasty decisions, spending impulsively, or having trouble waiting your turn?
I don't really experience those kinds of behaviors, to be honest. I haven't noticed myself making hasty decisions or spending money impulsively at all.
Can you think of one specific time recently when interrupting or blurting something out caused a problem at work, school, home, or with friends?

Yes, it actually happens quite often and is really frustrating. Just last week during a team meeting, I cut off my coworker and blurted out an answer before she could finish presenting her slide, which made her really annoyed with me. I just couldn't wait to share my thought, but it ended up creating a lot of tension between us.
Has this also caused problems outside of work, like with family or friends?

Yes, it definitely causes issues with my family and friends too. I often interrupt their conversations or butt into their activities, which really annoys them. They sometimes feel like I'm not listening to them because I talk so much.
